latest_release.name: TensorFold 1.3.4
latest_release.body:
# TensorFold 1.3.4

1.3.4 makes `tensorfold pull` work through proxies: it honours the proxy environment on every hop of a redirect, bounds every connect and read, and resumes a stalled file from its partial bytes. It hardens tool-call parsing and grammar compiles, which now bound their work, and cluster launch, session restore, Hub pulls and Web pairing now fail closed on malformed input; the `json_object` grammar is fixed to work on large vocabularies under the new limits. On CUDA, GLM at TP=2 does less work per prompt by default, and with `TF_GLM_PAIR_EXPERTS=1` its prompts are 15% faster at 2K on two GB10s, while the server takes `n` up to 16 and `cache_salt` and Ripple-65B-Preview runs on M5 Macs. This release is not slower than 1.3.3 anywhere: copy-only decode on AMD Strix Halo keeps 1.3.3's lone-stream copy pricing.

## Speed

- **Flash Next on Metal (M5):** the 4-bit expert scale and bias index is now built on Macs with tensor units too. One-stream decode is 2-5% faster on an M5 Ultra, with the same tokens (#4547).
- **Qwen3.8-27B on Intel GPUs (decode attention):** decode attention merges its slices with 16 subgroups a head instead of one, adding them in the same order, so every output byte is unchanged (token hashes match main, drafted and plain, bf16 and int8 KV). On an Arc Pro B70, plain decode gains 1.8 to 2.0% at about 8,000 prompt tokens, 14.7 to 16.0% at about 30,000 and 39.8 to 42.2% at 121,022. Drafted decode is level. The kernel contract registers it as a bit-equal replacement with two planted controls (#3960, lands #2799).
- **GLM on CUDA (TP=2 prompts):** when a chunk crosses the dense limit, dense attention runs only on the rows sparse attention leaves untouched. Prefill also skips projections nothing reads (the MTP proposal and query-side work). Outputs are unchanged (#4499).
- **GLM on CUDA (TP=2 paired experts):** opt-in `TF_GLM_PAIR_EXPERTS=1` runs one grouped routed-expert pass per prompt pair with 128-row items, so experts with many tokens read their weights once. Each rank passes its own FFN partial under the default split reduction, so tokens match the unpaired path. On two GB10s, prompts are 15% faster at 2K and about 5% faster at 8K and 32K. Off, nothing changes (#4493, #4619).
- **GLM on CUDA (TP=2 index split):** `TF_GLM_INDEX_SPLIT=32768` keeps indexer scores, pools and token rows local on each rank below that position, with no blocking all-gathers, and own partials are read in place. Outputs are unchanged, and the default stays 2048 (#4510).
- **GLM-5.3-Flash on CUDA (EXL3 experts):** `TF_GLM_MOE_DIRECT=1` (off by default) runs a decode window's EXL3 experts without their two row copies and the shared expert's slot write. It sums the slot rows bit-equal to the default path, so replies are unchanged (#3659, for #3570).
- **Flash Next on CUDA (fused split):** opt-in `TF_FLASHNEXT_FUSED_SPLIT=1` runs decode projections that split K over a cluster, at 2,048 output columns or more, on the fused form. It adds the K slices in the cluster's order, so the bits are unchanged. Unset, blank or `0` keeps the current kernels, and Metal and HIP refuse `1` at startup (#3475).
- **Flash Next on CUDA (n-gram gather):** `TF_FLASHNEXT_GATHER_EARLY=1` (default `0`) gathers a shared decode pass's n-gram rows for every lane in one pooled call instead of one call a stream, for passes of at most 64 lanes. Wider passes keep the per-stream call. Which rows are read and how a row is dequantized do not change, so replies are unchanged. The measured mean decode gain on one GB10 rises to +2.10% at eight streams (#4009).
- **Flash Next on CUDA (follow-up turns):** after a chat reply, a quiet background pass keeps its state, so the next turn resumes past the reply instead of prefilling it. The pass runs on one rank and yields when a request arrives (#3219).
- **HIP (DFlash2 holds):** a DFlash2 hold runs only the rows its drafts need: a frame takes its deepest stream's drafts plus the pending row, within the block. A draft's

Help Support TensorFold · @tensorfold_dev on X

# TensorFold TensorFold serves language models from a Zig binary on Apple Silicon and NVIDIA GPUs. The engine reads checkpoints, tokenizes requests and runs Metal or CUDA kernels directly. Serving needs no Python or MLX installation. Building with a coding agent? Have it load the [contributor skill](docs/recipes/SKILL.md) and follow [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md#contributing-with-agents). ## Quick start Start with Qwen3.5-2B, a small 4-bit checkpoint. The commands below download its pinned revision, then serve it as `local-model`. Model weights have their own licenses. ### Mac with Apple Silicon Install with Homebrew, then start the server: ```sh brew install ashhart/tensorfold/tensorfold tensorfold pull mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit@93760be4f1f69842a46bc13dbdc0f19e291392a3 tensorfold serve mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit --name local-model --context 8192 --no-thinking ``` ### Linux with an NVIDIA GPU Needs glibc 2.28 or newer and NVIDIA driver R580 or newer (CUDA 13.0). The [run guide](docs/run-guide.md#platform-setup) lists the archive's requirements; Windows has [its own guide](docs/WINDOWS.md). ```sh V=1.3.4 case "$(uname -m)" in aarch64|arm64) PLATFORM=linux-aarch64 ;; x86_64) PLATFORM=linux-x86_64 ;; *) echo 'No release archive for this CPU' >&2; exit 1 ;; esac curl -fLO "https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/releases/download/v$V/tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz" curl -fLO "https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/releases/download/v$V/tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz.sha256" sha256sum -c "tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz.sha256" tar -xzf "tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz" export PATH="$PWD/tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM/bin:$PATH" tensorfold() { command tensorfold-native "$@"; } tensorfold pull mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit@93760be4f1f69842a46bc13dbdc0f19e291392a3 tensorfold serve mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit --name local-model --context 8192 --no-thinking ``` ### Send a request Leave the server running. In another terminal, on either platform: ```sh curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"local-model","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello in one sentence."}],"max_tokens":128,"temperature":0}' ``` The API also serves completions, Responses and Anthropic Messages. `/v1/models` lists the served name. To talk to a model in the terminal in one command, `tensorfold chat MODEL` starts the server itself, streams each reply and stops the server when the chat ends; `/help` lists the chat's commands, and `/bye` or Ctrl-D ends it: ```sh tensorfold chat mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit ``` With the server above still running, `tensorfold chat --url http://127.0.0.1:8080` chats with it instead, and `echo "Say hello." | tensorfold chat --url http://127.0.0.1:8080` prints one reply for a script. See [the chat command](docs/chat.md) for its flags and the serve flags it passes on. ## Docs - [Run guide](docs/run-guide.md): platform setup, requests, parallel requests, exact decoding, context compaction, Cortheon mode, every serve flag, the Mac app and TensorFold Starlight. - [Supported models](docs/supported-models.md): which checkpoints run on which machines, models on disk and model discovery. - [Living Weights (experimental)](docs/living-weights.md): teach a running model new facts in its own weights. - [Installation runbook](RUNBOOK.md): macOS and CUDA installation, paired Metal serving and troubleshooting. - [Windows](docs/WINDOWS.md), [TensorFold Web](docs/web.md) and [the Mac app](app/README.md). - [API](docs/api.md), [Cortheon mode](docs/cortheon.md) and [known issues](docs/known-issues.md). - [Evaluating TensorFold](docs/evaluating.md) and [community benchmarks](docs/community-benchmarks.md). - [Usable memory profiles](docs/memory-profiling.md): how to record applied budgets, context, cache state and process peaks. - [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md): ATC and agents, builds, tests and the exactness and performance gates. - [Changes](CHANGELOG.md), [1.0.0 release notes](docs/release-notes-1.0.0.md) and [the Zig engine preview](docs/zig-preview.md). - TensorFold is Apache-2.0: [LICENSE](LICENSE), [NOTICE](NOTICE), [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) and [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## Contributors Thank you to everyone who has sent TensorFold a pull request, a measurement or a bug report:
